newsitem.title: USA: Army chief of staff says sex harass probe to widen.
newsitem.headline: Army chief of staff says sex harass probe to widen.

text.p: The U.S. Army Chief of Staff said Wednesday he expected the investigation into sexual harassment in his branch of the service would widen to include a number of bases.

Gen. Dennis Reimer, speaking to reporters after a meeting on defence sponsored by the Tufts School of Law and Diplomacy, said about 2,500 calls had been received at a hotline set up to investigate charges of sexual harassment in the six days since initial charges that a drill sergeant had raped a female trainee at the Aberdeen Proving Ground in Maryland.
"My guess is that it will probably widen," Reimer said when asked if the probe would be expanded.
He estimated that about 30 percent of the phone calls pertained to the problems at Aberdeen, while the remainder involved other military institutions.
Reimer vowed that the investigation would go to the highest ranks, saying, "We will get to the bottom of this. We will do whatever is necessary."
He said 234 calls had been referred to the criminal investigations unit.
"The fact is we have a few people who have tarnished the image of the (Army) but that does not reflect the U.S. Army that I am part of."
